dispositions.observation: Two orthographic views of the same object report different heights: front rendered_height_mm 113.64 (bounds y0=129, y1=2081 = 1952 px) versus side rendered_height_mm 114.23 (bounds y0=119, y1=2081 = 1962 px). For a body of revolution under an identical orthographic camera the two heights should agree. The cause is NOT determined here — asymmetry in the bulb or collar, and a mask-extraction edge difference, are both consistent with the evidence, and separating them is outside a review's authority. Widths themselves are within tolerance: 37.36 rendered against 37.4 contract is 0.04 mm, below one pixel.

closure_detail is framed off-centre and its subject is CLIPPED: bounds_px x0=115, x1=1217, y0=432, y1=2199 with touches_frame TRUE and closure_view_coverage 0.5532. The render manifest already warns RENDER_OFF_CENTER:closure_detail and the contact sheet prints that warning in red, so the package is honest about it — but the consequence for review is not cosmetic. The camera standard's comparison rule is 'identical camera, never differing zoom'; a view whose subject runs out of frame cannot be placed under that rule against any future reference photograph, so this view is not yet usable as comparison evidence. Recorded as perspective mismatch because it is a camera-framing defect and that is the closest category the contract defines; it is a framing fault, not a projection fault — every packaged view is orthographic as the standard requires.
